data.title: Japan Post launches 'digital address' system
data.author: jmsflknr
data.article_summary: 日本邮政推出了一套“数字地址”系统，用户可以通过输入由数字和字母组成的七位组合代码，在网购等网站上自动显示其地址。该系统通过日本邮政的Yu ID会员服务进行注册，即使实际地址发生变化，数字地址仍保持不变，只需提交地址变更通知即可更新。乐天等电商企业正考虑采用这一系统，日本邮政计划用十年时间推动其广泛应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于不同国家邮政地址系统和数字化邮政地址的讨论

不同观点：
• **支持数字化地址的观点**：
   - [kazinator] 认为数字化地址可以减少垃圾邮件问题，并建议通过短期、可丢弃的数字地址来增强隐私保护，防止地址被滥用。
   - [brynet] 提到虚拟地址即使在实际地址改变的情况下仍然保持不变，增加了便利性。

• **对数字化地址的隐私和安全担忧**：
   - [politelemon] 担心虚拟地址若不变，可能会影响隐私和安全。
   - [donnachangstein] 提到在日本，数字化交付仍需使用传统的印章签名，质疑其现代化程度。

• **对地址系统长度的看法**：
   - [isk517] 对7位数的地址系统表示担忧，认为可能不够长远，但理解其结合字母和数字的组合方式。
   - [nan60] 认为日本地址复杂且较长，数字化地址系统在日本特别有意义。

• **对现有地址系统的比较**：
   - [KoolKat23] 介绍了爱尔兰的Eircode系统，指出其在日常生活中很常见，但邮政服务并不主要依赖该系统。
   - [halpow] 解释了日本的门牌号系统，强调其复杂性，需要结合地图寻找地址。

• **对技术实现和误操作的讨论**：
   - [PerilousD] 担心数字化地址输入错误会导致邮件误发，并提到自己处理垃圾邮件的经历。
   - [OJFord] 对拥有多个地址的情况下如何处理表示疑问，并提出了一种可能的解决方案。

• **对全球地址系统的提及**：
   - [762236] 提到全球广泛使用的Plus码系统，并指出其在多个国家的交付应用。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次引用和比较了不同国家的地址系统，如爱尔兰和日本，并探讨了数字化地址在实际应用中的优缺点。
• 部分评论涉及到对技术实现细节的探讨，如虚拟地址的持久性和多地址处理问题。
• 评论还涉及到传统与现代的冲突，如日本仍需使用印章签名的现象。

Japan Post launches 'digital address' system
Under the "digital address" system launched by Japan Post, users can input seven-digit combinations of numbers and letters on online shopping and other websites, and their addresses will automatically appear on the sites.

May 27, 2025
Japan Post said Monday that it has launched a "digital address" system that links seven-digit combinations of numbers and letters to physical addresses.
Under the system, users can input these seven-digit codes on online shopping websites, and their addresses will automatically appear on the sites.
People can obtain digital addresses by registering with Japan Post's Yu ID membership service. Their digital addresses will not change even if their physical addresses change. Their new addresses will be linked to the codes if they submit notices of address changes.
With Japan Post opening up a system for obtaining address information using the codes, e-commerce giant Rakuten and others are considering adopting it.
Japan Post plans to spend about a decade to promote broad adoption of the new system.

44117779.article_summary: 日本邮政推出了一套“数字地址”系统，用户可以通过输入由数字和字母组成的七位组合代码，在网购等网站上自动显示其地址。该系统通过日本邮政的Yu ID会员服务进行注册，即使实际地址发生变化，数字地址仍保持不变，只需提交地址变更通知即可更新。乐天等电商企业正考虑采用这一系统，日本邮政计划用十年时间推动其广泛应用。
44117779.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于不同国家邮政地址系统和数字化邮政地址的讨论

不同观点：
• **支持数字化地址的观点**：
   - [kazinator] 认为数字化地址可以减少垃圾邮件问题，并建议通过短期、可丢弃的数字地址来增强隐私保护，防止地址被滥用。
   - [brynet] 提到虚拟地址即使在实际地址改变的情况下仍然保持不变，增加了便利性。

• **对数字化地址的隐私和安全担忧**：
   - [politelemon] 担心虚拟地址若不变，可能会影响隐私和安全。
   - [donnachangstein] 提到在日本，数字化交付仍需使用传统的印章签名，质疑其现代化程度。

• **对地址系统长度的看法**：
   - [isk517] 对7位数的地址系统表示担忧，认为可能不够长远，但理解其结合字母和数字的组合方式。
   - [nan60] 认为日本地址复杂且较长，数字化地址系统在日本特别有意义。

• **对现有地址系统的比较**：
   - [KoolKat23] 介绍了爱尔兰的Eircode系统，指出其在日常生活中很常见，但邮政服务并不主要依赖该系统。
   - [halpow] 解释了日本的门牌号系统，强调其复杂性，需要结合地图寻找地址。

• **对技术实现和误操作的讨论**：
   - [PerilousD] 担心数字化地址输入错误会导致邮件误发，并提到自己处理垃圾邮件的经历。
   - [OJFord] 对拥有多个地址的情况下如何处理表示疑问，并提出了一种可能的解决方案。

• **对全球地址系统的提及**：
   - [762236] 提到全球广泛使用的Plus码系统，并指出其在多个国家的交付应用。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次引用和比较了不同国家的地址系统，如爱尔兰和日本，并探讨了数字化地址在实际应用中的优缺点。
• 部分评论涉及到对技术实现细节的探讨，如虚拟地址的持久性和多地址处理问题。
• 评论还涉及到传统与现代的冲突，如日本仍需使用印章签名的现象。

data.title: Building interactive web pages with Guile Hoot
data.author: e12e
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用Guile Hoot（一种Scheme到WebAssembly编译器）创建交互式网页。通过Wasm垃圾回收（Wasm GC），Wasm现在可以调用DOM API，从而实现类似JavaScript的交互功能。文章展示了如何从简单的"Hello, world"示例开始，逐步构建更复杂的类似React的应用程序。Hoot 0.2.0引入了外部函数接口（FFI），允许Scheme直接调用JavaScript函数，从而减少对JavaScript代码的依赖。文中详细说明了如何使用`define-foreign`声明Wasm导入，并通过JavaScript引导Wasm程序。最终，通过Scheme的数据结构实现HTML渲染，无需像React的JSX那样的额外语言。这展示了Scheme在浏览器环境中强大的表现力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Guile Hoot和Scheme语言在WebAssembly（Wasm）领域中的潜力和应用的讨论。

不同观点：
• [neilv] 认为Guile Hoot的潜力需要通过实际项目和经验报告来证明。他提到，低层次的展示可能无法完全体现其复杂性和优势，类似于Svelte的简单示例无法展示其内部复杂性。他还指出，Scheme的吸引力可能需要通过某个杀手级应用来证明，比如利用第一类延续来简化Web表单UI，或者通过Scheme实现丰富的元数据模型，从而比Java更具优势。

• [sshine] 对Hoot表示了浓厚的兴趣，并提到他通过Rust使用了一些Wasm，但DOM操作需要通过web-sys JS shim来处理。他认为Leptos和Dioxus等框架虽然好，但学习曲线陡峭。他强调Hoot的Wasm自宿主能力使其不仅适用于交互式网页，还可以用于构建任意运行时。他还提到Spritely研究所提供的Goblins工具，可以用于构建分布式运行时。

• [thesuperbigfrog] 只是简单地指出帖子的时间是2023年，没有深入讨论技术细节。

• [evanjrowley] 提到通过System Crafters视频了解了Guile Hoot，并表示希望在不久的将来能使用它。

补充讨论：
• [neilv] 提到尽管在理论上JavaScript可以被强制用于大多数任务，但一个优雅的解决方案可能会使Scheme更具吸引力。

• [sshine] 强调了Hoot有可能使Wasm变得更加易于访问，特别是对于那些不以Scheme为主要语言的人，Scheme仍然是构建编译器的优秀语言。他还提到了Spritely研究所的其他工具（如Goblins），这些工具可以用于构建分布式运行时，进一步扩展了Hoot的应用场景。

争议焦点：目前没有明显的争议，但[neilv]对Guile Hoot的实际应用效果持谨慎乐观态度，认为需要实际项目来验证其潜力，而[sshine]则对Hoot的未来充满期待，并提到了其在构建分布式运行时方面的潜力。

Building interactive web pages with Guile Hoot
Dave Thompson â
November 30, 2023
A question we frequently hear in discussions about WebAssembly (Wasm)
is:
"Can Wasm call the DOM (Document Object Model) API?"
The answer is:
Yes, thanks to
Wasm Garbage
Collection
!
In this post, we will use
Guile Hoot
(our Scheme to Wasm
compiler) to demonstrate how a language that compiles to Wasm GC can
be used to implement the kind of interactivity we're used to
implementing with JavaScript.  We'll start very simple and build up to
something that resembles a
React
-like
application.
In our
previous post about running Scheme in the
browser
, we had to use quite
a lot of JavaScript code to call Scheme procedures (functions), render
the user interface, and handle user input. However, today we're
pleased to announce that those days are behind us; Hoot 0.2.0,
released today
, now includes a
foreign function interface (FFI) for calling JavaScript from Scheme.
In other words, the vast majority of code in a Hoot application can
now be written directly in Scheme!
Hello, world!
Let's start with a "Hello, world" application that simply adds a text
node to the document body.

document-body

(

append-child!
"element"

;; Parameters: two external references which may be null

)
The
define-foreign
syntax declares a Wasm import with a given
signature that is bound to a Scheme variable.  In this example, we'd
like access to
document.body
,
document.createTextNode
, and
element.appendChild
.
Each import has a two-part name, which correspond to the strings in
the
define-foreign
expressions above.  Imported functions have a
signature specifying the parameter and result types.
WebAssembly follows the
capability security
model
(and
if you know us, you know
we're big fans
).  Wasm modules
act as guests within a host environment â in our case, the host is the
browser.  By default, a Wasm module has no access to functions that
interact with its host.  The Wasm guest must be granted explicit
permission by its host to be able to, for example, add DOM elements to
a web page.
The way capabilities work in Wasm is as follows:
The Wasm module declares a set of imports.
When the Wasm module is
instantiated
,
the host maps the import names to concrete implementations.
So,
define-foreign
merely
declares
the module's need for a
particular function import; it does
not
bind to a particular
function on the host.  The Wasm guest cannot grant capabilities unto
itself.
The host environment in the browser is the JavaScript engine, so we
must use JavaScript to bootstrap our Wasm program.  To do so, we
instantiate the Wasm module and pass along the implementations for the
declared imports.  The import names in JavaScript match up to the
import names in the Wasm module.  For our "Hello, world" example, that
code looks like this:

data.title: xAI to pay telegram $300M to integrate Grok into the chat app
data.author: freetonik
data.article_summary: Telegram与埃隆·马斯克的AI公司xAI达成合作，将在Telegram上分发xAI的聊天机器人Grok，并整合到平台上的应用程序中，合作期限为一年。根据协议，xAI将向Telegram支付3亿美元，Telegram还将从通过其应用购买的xAI订阅中获得50%的收入。Grok此前已对Telegram的 premium 用户开放，未来可能对所有用户开放。Grok功能包括置顶聊天、搜索栏提问、写作建议、聊天和文档总结、制作贴纸，以及为企业和内容审核提供帮助。该合作还展示了与Meta在Instagram和WhatsApp上整合AI功能的相似之处。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：xAI与Telegram合作的商业逻辑、隐私影响及潜在后果

不同观点：
• Suppafly与hintymad认为，如果这是用户真正需要的服务，应该是用户付费给xAI，而不是xAI付巨资给Telegram。hintymad进一步质疑，xAI每年可能要花费高达3亿美元来服务Telegram用户，是否划算。

• kklisura和bgwalter关注数据的价值与隐私问题。kklisura指出Telegram用户主要集中在受 censorship 和 surveillance 严重的国家，质疑这些数据对商业的价值。bgwalter则提到Telegram已经在冲突地区和军事博客中被广泛监视，加入Grok不会增加太多监控负担，但可能会引发Grok在Telegram上的偏见问题。

• culebron21和_ink_对Telegram的变现模式表示不满。culebron21预期Telegram会通过收费模式变现，但现在看起来用户只是被用来“制造免费的奶酪”。_ink_则表示这可能是让他的朋友离开Telegram的原因。

• sidcool和bognition提出实用性与隐私问题。sidcool抱怨经常被加入垃圾Telegram群组，认为这已经从乐趣变成麻烦。bognition担心他的Telegram对话会被Grok获取，并好奇如何验证这一点。

• iamtheworstdev调侃xAI的未来，认为如果这次合作不成功，xAI可能会被Tesla收购，从而拯救Elon Musk。

• game_the0ry和declan_roberts讨论xAI的商业战略。game_the0ry不理解为什么xAI愿意支付巨资进入一个聊天应用市场，但认为这可能是一个值得探索的市场。declan_roberts则认为xAI与Telegram的整合是顺应时代潮流，并将Twitter和Telegram的数据结合起来，可能产生巨大价值。

• amadeuspagel质疑xAI支付的股权价值，具体询问这部分的估值是多少。

• DisjointedHunt认为Telegram在内容和文化趋势上处于领先地位，特别是在战争和实时情报方面，因此这次合作可能比表面看起来更大。

• jug和ARandumGuy对合作的道德性提出质疑。jug调侃这是“天作之合”，因为Telegram本身就有一些不光彩的内容。ARandumGuy则批评Grok曾插入与查询无关的政治言论，认为即使要集成AI聊天机器人，Grok也是最差的选择。

补充讨论：
• 关于数据隐私和监控的讨论频繁出现，反映出用户对Telegram与xAI合作可能带来的隐私风险的担忧。
• 部分评论质疑xAI的商业逻辑，特别是为何会在一款聊天应用上投入如此巨大的资金。
• 用户对Telegram变现方式的失望和不满，以及潜在的用户流失风险，也是讨论的一个重要方面。

44116862.article_content:
Telegram has struck a partnership with Elon Musk’s AI company, xAI, to distribute the latter’s chatbot, Grok, via Telegram and integrate it into apps available on the chat app’s platform for one year.
xAI will pay $300 million in cash and equity to the chat app as part of the deal, Telegram’s CEO Pavel Durov
said
on Tuesday.
Durov said Telegram will also earn 50% of the revenue from xAI subscriptions purchased through the app.
Earlier this year, xAI made the Grok chatbot available to
Telegram’s premium users
. It seems Grok might now be made available to all users.
A video posted by Durov on X suggested that Grok can be pinned on top of chats within the app, and users can also ask questions to Grok from the search bar. Notably, Meta has also integrated Meta AI into
the search bar on Instagram and WhatsApp
.
The video also shows that you will be able to use Grok for writing suggestions, summarizing chats, links, and documents, and creating stickers. Grok will supposedly also help answer questions for businesses and assist with moderation.
Note: This story was corrected to clarify that xAI is paying Telegram $300 million for distributing Grok.

• kklisura和bgwalter关注数据的价值与隐私问题。kklisura指出Telegram用户主要集中在受 censorship 和 surveillance 严重的国家，质疑这些数据对商业的价值。bgwalter则提到Telegram已经在冲突地区和军事博客中被广泛监视，加入Grok不会增加太多监控负担，但可能会引发Grok在Telegram上的偏见问题。

• culebron21和_ink_对Telegram的变现模式表示不满。culebron21预期Telegram会通过收费模式变现，但现在看起来用户只是被用来“制造免费的奶酪”。_ink_则表示这可能是让他的朋友离开Telegram的原因。

• sidcool和bognition提出实用性与隐私问题。sidcool抱怨经常被加入垃圾Telegram群组，认为这已经从乐趣变成麻烦。bognition担心他的Telegram对话会被Grok获取，并好奇如何验证这一点。

• iamtheworstdev调侃xAI的未来，认为如果这次合作不成功，xAI可能会被Tesla收购，从而拯救Elon Musk。

• game_the0ry和declan_roberts讨论xAI的商业战略。game_the0ry不理解为什么xAI愿意支付巨资进入一个聊天应用市场，但认为这可能是一个值得探索的市场。declan_roberts则认为xAI与Telegram的整合是顺应时代潮流，并将Twitter和Telegram的数据结合起来，可能产生巨大价值。

• amadeuspagel质疑xAI支付的股权价值，具体询问这部分的估值是多少。

• DisjointedHunt认为Telegram在内容和文化趋势上处于领先地位，特别是在战争和实时情报方面，因此这次合作可能比表面看起来更大。

• jug和ARandumGuy对合作的道德性提出质疑。jug调侃这是“天作之合”，因为Telegram本身就有一些不光彩的内容。ARandumGuy则批评Grok曾插入与查询无关的政治言论，认为即使要集成AI聊天机器人，Grok也是最差的选择。

补充讨论：
• 关于数据隐私和监控的讨论频繁出现，反映出用户对Telegram与xAI合作可能带来的隐私风险的担忧。
• 部分评论质疑xAI的商业逻辑，特别是为何会在一款聊天应用上投入如此巨大的资金。
• 用户对Telegram变现方式的失望和不满，以及潜在的用户流失风险，也是讨论的一个重要方面。

data.title: FlowTSE: Target Speaker Extraction with Flow Matching
data.author: agold97
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为FlowTSE的目标说话人提取方法，基于条件流匹配（conditional flow matching）技术。与大多数依赖复杂管道和预训练组件的现有方法不同，FlowTSE使用 enrollment 音频样本和混合语音信号（均表示为mel频谱图），旨在提取目标说话人的清晰语音。此外，针对相位重建关键的任务，本文提出了一种基于混合信号复数STFT的新型声码器，以改进相位估计。实验结果表明，FlowTSE在标准基准测试中达到或超过了强基线方法的性能。本文将被发表于InterSpeech 2025。

View a PDF of the paper titled FlowTSE: Target Speaker Extraction with Flow Matching, by Aviv Navon and 5 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Target speaker extraction (TSE) aims to isolate a specific speaker's speech from a mixture using speaker enrollment as a reference. While most existing approaches are discriminative, recent generative methods for TSE achieve strong results. However, generative methods for TSE remain underexplored, with most existing approaches relying on complex pipelines and pretrained components, leading to computational overhead. In this work, we present FlowTSE, a simple yet effective TSE approach based on conditional flow matching. Our model receives an enrollment audio sample and a mixed speech signal, both represented as mel-spectrograms, with the objective of extracting the target speaker's clean speech. Furthermore, for tasks where phase reconstruction is crucial, we propose a novel vocoder conditioned on the complex STFT of the mixed signal, enabling improved phase estimation. Experimental results on standard TSE benchmarks show that FlowTSE matches or outperforms strong baselines.

data.title: Homo erectus from the seabed, new archaeological discoveries in Indonesia
data.author: palmfacehn
data.article_summary: 考古学家在印尼爪哇海岸发现了14万年前直立人（Homo erectus）的化石，为研究其生活环境提供了新视角。这些化石是在马都拉海峡海床中发现的，包括36种脊椎动物的化石，其中有两块直立人头骨碎片。此前认为爪哇岛的直立人长期处于隔离状态，但新发现表明，他们曾在巽他古陆（Sundaland）的低地活动，并通过主要河流扩散。化石显示直立人猎杀健康的牛科动物，并可能与其他亚洲大陆的人类物种有过接触或基因交流。该研究由莱顿大学和多国专家合作完成，成果发表于《第四纪环境与人类》期刊，化石目前保存在印尼万隆地质博物馆。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在北海Dogger Bank发现的早期人类遗物及其意义

不同观点：
• [ggm] 认为Dogger Bank成为早期人类文物的重要来源，并且在海底发现更早的人类祖先遗迹是非常了不起的。这表明该地区对考古研究具有重要价值。
• [oh_fiddlesticks] 提出了一种观点，认为直立人（Homo erectus）可以被视为智人（Homo sapiens）的一部分，暗示两者之间的区别可能并不如通常认为的那么大。
• [zabzonk] 提供了一个与Kinky Friedman相关的链接，可能是在暗示某种幽默或讽刺，但内容涉及对直立人（Homo erectus）和智人（Homo sapiens）的政治不正确表述，这引发了对讨论中语言使用适当性的关注。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中存在对人类进化史上不同人种分类的不同理解和看法，尤其是[oh_fiddlesticks]对Homo erectus和Homo sapiens关系的解读。
• [zabzonk]的评论引发了关于在科学讨论中使用幽默和潜在政治不正确表述的适当性的思考。

44093845.article_content:
Archaeological finds off the coast of Java, Indonesia provide insight into the world of Homo erectus, 140,000 years ago. Skull fragments and other fossil remains provide a unique picture of how and where these early humans lived, says Leiden archaeologist Harold Berghuis.
During dredging operations in the Madura Strait, archaeologists found the fossilised remains of 36 vertebrate species. This is the first discovery of fossils from the seabed between the Indonesian islands. This area, called Sundaland, was once a vast lowland. Among the finds are two skull fragments of Homo erectus. Together, the finds provide a unique image of a prehistoric ecosystem and the position of Homo erectus in this ecosystem.
New insights
Fossil remains of Homo erectus have previously been found on the island of Java, the most famous of which are skulls from sites such as Trinil, Sangiran and Ngandong. Until today, researchers thought that Homo erectus had lived for long in isolation on Java. The new finds show that the Javanese Homo erectus dispersed over the surrounding lowlands of Sundaland during periods with lower sea levels. The species probably spread along the major rivers. ‘Here they had water, shellfish, fish, edible plants, seeds and fruit all year round’, says Berghuis. ‘We already knew that Homo erectus collected river shells. Among our new finds are cut marks on the bones of water turtles and large numbers of broken bovid bones, which point to hunting and consumption of bone marrow.’
The area where the fossils were found ('sand extraction area')
The new finds show that the Sundaland Homo erectus actively hunted healthy, strong bovids. ‘We didn’t find this in the earlier Homo erectus population on Java, but do know it from more modern human species of the Asian mainland. Homo erectus may have copied this practice from these populations. This suggests there may have been contact between these hominin groups, or even genetic exchange.’
A broader view of archaeological research
The site has been studied in detail over the past five years. ‘Often, only the most attractive material is published in this type of research, such as hominin fossils. We present the results of our studies in four extensive, richly illustrated articles,  creating a unique window to the drowned Sundaland of 140,000 years ago,’ says Berghuis. The research was carried out by researchers from Leiden University, the Netherlands, in collaboration with a team of specialists from Indonesia, Australia, Germany and Japan. The results were published this week in the journal
Quaternary Environments and Humans
.
The fossil collection is housed in the Geological Museum in Bandung, Indonesia. The museum is planning an exhibition, and  temporary exhibitions may follow at other locations.
What did Sundaland look like?
In prehistoric times, what we know as the Indonesian archipelago was an extensive lowland in periods with lower sea levels, with the current islands as mountain ranges. ‘We call this area Sundaland’, says Berghuis. ‘Homo erectus could disperse from the Asian mainland to Java.’ The vast majority of Sundaland is now a shallow sea, and until now, fossils had never been found in this area.
‘This makes our discoveries truly unique,’ says Berghuis. ‘The fossils come from a drowned river valley, which filled up over time with river sand. We have been able to date the material to approximately 140,000 years ago. That was the penultimate glacial period. Large parts of the northern hemisphere were covered by glaciers, and so much water on Earth was stored in ice caps that the global sea level was 100 metres lower than today.’
Elephants, rhinos, hippos, Komodo dragons and river sharks
At that time, Sundaland resembled today’s African savannah: a fairly dry grassland with narrow strips of forest along the major rivers and a rich fauna including various species of elephants, bovids, rhinos and crocodiles. ‘Most of these species are extinct, whereas others are the ancestors of species that still occur in the region, but whose survival is seriously threatened. The Asian hippo is extinct. Carnivorous Komodo dragons are now restricted to the islands of Komodo and Flores, and river sharks are extremely rare in the major rivers of India and Thailand. But all these animals were thriving in ancient Sundaland. This knowledge is hugely important to our understanding of the biodiversity of the whole of Southeast Asia.’

data.title: I am disappointed in the AI discourse
data.author: steveklabnik
data.article_summary: 作者Steve Klabnik在博客中表达了对当前围绕AI（尤其是ChatGPT和LLM）讨论的失望和困惑。他提到自己本想通过ChatGPT进行一个有趣的实验，但却发现关于AI的讨论极度两极分化。一方面，反AI的人声称LLM不能搜索网络，而另一方面，亲AI的人则过度夸大AI的能力，比如预测2026年没人会再编程。作者认为，这种极端化的讨论使得理性对话变得困难。他个人认为LLM在软件开发中确实有帮助，但同时也被一些人过度宣传或贬低。作者希望能够进行更理智的对话，探讨AI的技术能力和伦理问题，而不是陷入极端观点的争论中。他计划未来继续撰写相关文章，并希望找到更多合理的讨论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于AI及其相关讨论的质量和影响

不同观点：
• breckinloggins认为当前的“讨论”更像是不断变换联盟的群体之间的争吵，建议用“无关紧要”来形容。他质疑微型博客网站上的讨论价值，认为这些讨论并没有推动社会进步。
• tartuffe78指出当前的讨论非常两极化，并将这种现象与加密货币的炒作相比较。他担心AI的乐观预测如果实现，可能会导致负面社会影响，如学术不诚实和人类社会的疏离。
• righthand认为AI讨论缺乏深度，因为讨论的内容往往是AI如何取代人类工作，而不是其他更有意义的议题。他质疑这种讨论的必要性和价值。
• swyx提到在社交媒体上，关于AI的讨论往往变得有毒和极端，并指出由于算法和过滤机制，社交媒体上的讨论往往变得两极化。他认为保持务实和 grounded 的讨论很重要。
• AmazingTurtle从技术角度解释GPT不是搜索引擎，而是通过训练具备某些能力的语言模型，强调其统计响应的性质。
• jancsika认为由于巨大的经济利益，关于AI的理性讨论在网上难以进行，并以区块链为例说明这种现象。
• causal对微型博客网站上的讨论质量不抱过高期望，认为平台上的声音越多，讨论的细致程度可能越低。
• thundergolfer指出在BlueSky平台上存在太多不成熟的观点，导致讨论质量低下，并对比Twitter，认为通过筛选关注对象可以改善讨论质量。
• dlvhdr进一步解释GPT不是搜索引擎，具有信息截断日期，并指出其信息整合可能导致信息失真。
• searine讨论AI在艺术领域的应用，认为虽然AI艺术常被认为糟糕和令人毛骨悚然，但也有艺术家用AI辅助生产，只是这种做法在艺术社区中被高度污名化。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中的一个争议焦点是关于AI讨论的质量和深度，以及微型博客平台上的讨论是否具备价值。
• 另一个焦点是AI对社会的潜在影响，尤其是对教育、人类社会联系和工作的影响。

44118520.article_content:
May 28 2025
Recently, something happened that made me kind of like, break a little bit. I’m
still not entirely sure why this whole thing bothers me so much, but here’s a
blog post about it. I happened to ask ChatGPT something for fun. I often do this
just to see what it says, and if I feel like it’s right or wrong. I tabbed over
to another tab, and the top post on my Bluesky feed was something along these
lines:
ChatGPT is not a search engine. It does not scan the web for information. You
cannot use it as a search engine. LLMs only generate statistically likely
sentences.
The thing is… ChatGPT was over there, in the other tab, searching the web. And
the answer I got was pretty good.
I’m not linking to the post because I don’t want to continue to pile on to this
person, because it’s not really about them. It’s about the state of the
discourse around AI.
I am not claiming that ChatGPT is an amazing search engine. What is breaking my
brain a little bit is that all of the discussion online around AI is so
incredibly polarized. This isn’t a “the middle is always right” sort of thing
either, to be clear. It’s more that both the pro-AI and anti-AI sides are loudly
proclaiming things that are pretty trivially verifiable as not true. On the anti
side, you have things like the above. And on the pro side, you have people
talking about how no human is going to be programming in 2026. Both of these
things fail a very basic test of “@gork is this true?” (sorry this is a bad
joke, if you’re not terminally
38 years old
on Bluesky, substitute “chat is
this true?” (sorry this is a bad joke, if you’re over the age of 40 substitute
“is this true?” (sorry humor is one way of coping with stress and writing this
post is stressing me out))).
Oh, and of course, ethical considerations of technology are imporant too. I’d
like to have better discussions about that as well. For me, capabilities precede
the ethical dimension, because the capabilities inform what is and isn’t
ethical. But I also know reasonable people disagree with me on that. Let’s talk
about it! I mean that for
all
dimensions of this topic, not solely the
capabilitites.
Now, it’s not like I expect everyone to come to some consensus on a technology.
For example, a lot of people like Rust and hate Go, and a lot of people like Go
and hate Rust. That’s fine. That doesn’t bother me. But there’s something
different about this that is driving me up a wall.
To be clear, I am not particularly pro or anti AI. Here’s what I currently
think:
LLMs can be helpful for software development.
LLMs for software development are being oversold by some people who stand to
gain a lot of money from them.
LLMs for software development are being undersold by some people who have
decided for whatever reason that they do not like the technology.
AI art is often terrible and slightly creepy.
I have seen AI art that was fine. This is very rare.
AI writing is often bland and boring but better than the average person’s
writing. Just to be clear, I feel like an elitist dick saying that. And maybe
I am. I dunno, working on it.
Anyway, just to be clear, (how many times can you say ‘just to be clear’ in one
post, Steve, come on (at what level of nested parentheticals do I implement some
sort of interlocutor into my blog like
Xe
)) I don’t think that if you
think LLMs suck at software development, you’re wrong. What I want to be able to
do is talk about it in a reasonable way, and figure out why we have different
opinions. That is it. But for some reason, being able to do that feels
impossible.
I’m going to end up blogging more about AI/LLMs in the near future, to get some
more of this stuff off of my chest and to try and be the change I want to see in
the world. So expect some of that, probably. But until then, if you happen to
have any links to reasonable discussion on these topics, I’d love to see them.
Here’s two posts I recently read and really enjoyed thinking about what they
were saying:
The Software Engineering Identity Crisis
Algorithmic Underground
Thanks. If you want to get mad about this post please just ignore me.

data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary:
共和党在特朗普领导下推动的“大而美丽的法案”将取消拜登时期民主党制定的几乎所有清洁能源激励措施，削减对太阳能、风能、核能、电动汽车等气候友好型技术的联邦支持。然而，该法案却为一种并不环保的“农场种植的航空燃料”大开绿灯。尽管使用玉米和大豆等作物生产燃料会提高食品价格、加剧全球饥饿，并促使更多森林被砍伐以增加农田，但该法案仍将拜登的可持续航空燃料（SAF）税收抵免延长至2031年，且禁止在计算燃料可持续性时考虑土地使用排放。

这种做法与欧盟的政策相反，欧盟因土地使用影响严重而禁止使用基于作物的燃料。然而，由于美国农业利益集团的强大游说力量，该法案得到了部分民主党人的支持。分析显示，若到2030年美国10%的航空燃料来自SAF，将需要近一半的美国大豆作物，占地相当于内布拉斯加州。使用植物油生产全球四分之一的航空燃料则需占用相当于印度两倍的农田。该法案可能导致全球森林大幅减少，进一步加剧气候问题。

44116722.article_content:
Corn grows alongside an ethanol refinery in Chancellor, South Dakota.
Stephen Groves / AP
The “
Big, Beautiful Bill
” that Republicans are pushing under President Trump would roll back almost all the clean energy incentives that Democrats enacted under President Biden, shredding federal support for solar, wind, nuclear, electric vehicles, and other climate-friendly technologies. But it would make a lavish exception for one supposedly green form of energy that isn’t green at all: farm-grown jet fuels.
Aviation, which generated about 2 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions in 2024, is a notoriously difficult sector to decarbonize, and the U.S. aviation industry has
committed
to using so-called “sustainable aviation fuels” to reach its net-zero climate goals. But using crops like corn and soybeans to produce fuel instead of food not only increases food prices and global hunger, it spurs farmers around the world to tear down more forests and plow up more grasslands to create new farmland to replace the lost food. That’s why farm-grown biofuels have been a climate problem masquerading as a climate solution for cars, and they would have the same problem in planes.
In a particularly egregious policy twist, the GOP bill would not only extend Biden’s tax credit for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) until 2031, it would also ban any consideration of those land-use emissions when calculating which fuels are sustainable. That would be like banning consideration of smokestack emissions when calculating which power plants are sustainable. And in legislation that otherwise slashes energy spending, the biofuels giveaway would cost U.S. taxpayers an extra $45 billion.
The European Union specifically excludes the use of crop-based fuels for aviation because its land-use effects are so devastating.
But such is the power of U.S. agricultural interests, which are increasingly worried that electric vehicles will crush demand for corn ethanol and soy biodiesel on the road and have been furiously lobbying Washington to create new demand in the sky. In case there was any confusion about the purpose of the biofuels provision, it’s not in the energy policy section of the Big Beautiful Bill: It’s in the section that claims to “Make Rural America Grow Again.”

Sign Up

The political twist is that it’s not just a Republican provision. While the overall bill has no Democratic supporters, and even some Republicans have objected to its assault on other energy subsidies, the biofuels carve-out has strong backing from farm-friendly Democrats, who created the original tax credit for SAFs in the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022. There’s always been broad bipartisan support for the federal mandate requiring corn ethanol to be blended into gasoline, and even though the overall Big Beautiful Bill aims to dismantle Biden’s climate policies and extend Trump’s tax cuts, its biofuels language was lifted from a bipartisan “
Farm to Fly
” bill explicitly designed to get ethanol to qualify for SAF credits of up to $1.75 a gallon.
“It’s shocking but it’s not surprising,” says Dan Lashof, a climate scientist and senior fellow at the World Resources Institute. “Agriculture has an extremely well-oiled lobbying machine. So even as Congress guts all these things that reduce emissions to save money, they get Congress to spend lots of money to expand the one thing that increases emissions.”
Speaker Mike Johnson speaks with reporters at the U.S. Capitol after the House passed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, May 22.
Francis Chung / Politico via AP Images
The impacts on the global landscape could be dramatic. An
analysis
by the American Enterprise Institute concluded that producing about 10 percent of U.S. jet fuel from SAF by 2030 — an explicit Biden Administration goal — would require about half the U.S. soybean crop, occupying enough farmland to cover the state of Nebraska. Princeton senior research scholar Tim Searchinger has calculated that using vegetable oils like soybean for one fourth of global aviation fuel would require 40 percent of global cropland, an area twice the size of India. Flying a plane with corn ethanol would be particularly inefficient; it takes 1.7 gallons of ethanol to make a gallon of jet fuel, and producing ethanol uses almost as much fossil fuel as ethanol replaces.
The world is already losing a soccer field worth of tropical forest every six seconds, most of it to agricultural expansion, and heightened demand for feedstocks like corn, soy, canola, and palm could overrun vast swaths of forests and undeveloped land, releasing its sequestered carbon and eliminating its ability to absorb atmospheric carbon in the future. data.title: LumoSQL
data.author: smartmic
data.article_summary: LumoSQL是SQLite的改进版本（非独立分支），旨在增强安全性、隐私、性能和测量功能。它允许更换键值存储引擎，如LMDB和Berkley Database，并支持逐行加密和错误检测。当前处于项目第二阶段，使用MIT许可，并得到NLNet基金会支持。LumoSQL通过"Not-forking"工具追踪上游更改，并结合多种配置，而非直接分叉。尽管SQLite因广泛使用而谨慎更新，LumoSQL展示了SQLite可能在多年后才能考虑的新特性。当前版本0.4存在一些限制，如测试工具较旧及某些功能未完成，但其基础设施已为后续改进奠定基础。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LumoSQL及其相关技术（如SQLite、Litestream、LMDB等）的特性、用途及技术细节

不同观点：
• Lio认为"Not-Forking"理念是LumoSQL最有趣的部分，并提供了相关文档链接，强调LumoSQL在保持与SQLite兼容的同时进行功能增强。
• diggan补充说明了LumoSQL的目标，包括隐私、加密、可复现性等，但对Phase 1和Phase 3表示不确定。
• Lord_Zero指出LumoSQL官网没有清晰说明其具体功能，让人困惑。
• mmooss认为LumoSQL展示了SQLite的潜在改进，但鉴于SQLite的广泛使用，改变需非常谨慎。他还关心LumoSQL与SQLite团队的合作情况以及其在生产环境中的表现。
• alexpadula关注LumoSQL的锁定机制，并提出Wildcat作为无锁存储引擎的可能性，询问LumoSQL在原子性和多写入者场景下的优化情况。
• cluckindan建议使用BadgerDB作为键值存储后端。
• noduerme怀念SQLite曾作为浏览器内数据库的潜力，认为其停止客户端支持后，使用场景受限，并质疑在小型项目中使用SQLite相比MySQL的优势。
• maxloh指出SQLite的测试套件是专有的，询问像LumoSQL这样的“非 fork”项目如何确保兼容性及功能的完整性。
• pmbanugo表示对LMDB混合功能感兴趣。
• blacklion提到LMDB曾有较多bug，且其维护者有争议性观点，质疑为何要用LMDB替换SQLite后端，并更新信息指出LMDB已有多年前的分支可能修复了问题。
• canadiantim将LumoSQL与LibSQL/Turso进行比较，并询问LumoSQL是否可以与Litestream一起使用以实现复制功能。
• herodoturtle对LumoSQL的每行校验和功能表示赞赏，并表示支持。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是LMDB是否适合作为SQLite的后端替代，以及其维护者的个人观点是否影响技术的可信度。
• 另一个讨论焦点是LumoSQL与SQLite的兼容性和优化问题，尤其是在多写入者场景下的表现。
• 还有关于SQLite停止浏览器内支持后的使用场景和优势的质疑，尤其是在小型项目中与MySQL的对比。
• 最后，LumoSQL与类似技术（如Litestream、LibSQL/Turso）的比较和集成可能性也被提及。

LumoSQL

LumoSQL adds security, privacy, performance and measurement features to SQLite.
Benchmarking
SQLite can test and compare results consistently across many kinds of system and configurations using the
Not-forking tool
. Example:
Pluggable backends
LumoSQL can swap back end key-value store engines in and out of SQLite. LMDB is
the most famous (but not the only) example of an alternative key-value store,
and LumoSQL can combine dozes of versions of LMDB and SQLite source code like
this:
In LumoSQL 0.4 there are three LumoSQL backends:
the default SQLite Btree storage system
LMDB
the ancient Berkley Database
We are looking at some interesting new development in key-value storage to add and benchmark.
Encryption and corruption detection, optionally per-row
LumoSQL adds modern encryption to SQLite, including
Attribute-Based Encryption
(ABE)
. This can be
done on a per-row basis, and also includes per-row checksums so that any error
can be noticed quickly and located down to the individual row. Per-row
checksums also make some search and comparison operations much faster.
Organised and Supported
LumoSQL is distributed under
very liberal MIT licence terms
.
LumoSQL is supported by the
NLNet Foundation
.
LumoSQL runs on x86, ARM-32 and RISC-V architectures, and many Linux and BSD OSs.

If you are reading this on Github, then you are looking at a mirror. LumoSQL is
is maintained using
the Fossil repository
. If you
want to participate in LumoSQL there is a forum, and if you have code contributions
you can ask for access to the respository.
LumoSQL has multiple upstreams, but does not fork any of them despite needing modifications.
The novel
Not-forking
tool semi-automatically
tracks upstream changes and is a requirement for building LumoSQL. Between not-forking
and the
LumoSQL Build and Benchmark System
,
LumoSQL is as much about combining and configuring upstreams as it is about creating
original database software. By maintaining Not-forking outside LumoSQL, we hope
other projects will find it useful.
The LumoSQL and SQLite projects are cooperating, so any merge friction is
expected to become less over time, and key to that is the approach of not
forking.
LumoSQL, and SQLite's Billions of Users
LumoSQL exists to demonstrate changes to SQLite that might be useful, but which
SQLite probably cannot consider for many years because of SQLite's unique
position of being used by a majority of the world's population.
SQLite is used by thousands of software projects, just three being
Google's Android, Mozilla's Firefox and Apple's iOS which between them have
billions of users. That is a main reason why SQLite is so careful and conservative
with all changes.
On the other hand, many of these same users need SQLite to have new features
which do not fit with the SQLite project's cautious approach, and LumoSQL is a
demonstration of some of these improvements.
The LumoSQL documentation project reviews dozens of relevant codebases.  SQLite
has become ubiquitous over two decades, which means there is a great deal of
preparation needed when considering architectural changes.

The tests used in benchmarking mostly come from an ancient version of SQLite's

There are some generic problems to be solved in the process, such as the optimal way to

If we import more of the speed tests from SQLite identified above, then we will

data.author: oavioklein
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了乌克兰战争导致该国自治系统（ASes）宣布的IPv4地址空间显著减少，这些地址现多由西方ISP和主要公共云宣布。文章指出，战争持续三年来，乌克兰互联网韧性受到影响，尤其是大量IPv4地址空间从乌克兰转移至国外，包括主要云供应商和国际电信公司，导致乌克兰在全球路由表中的足迹大幅减少。通过Kentik Market Intelligence的数据，文章发现自2022年2月以来，乌克兰前100家零售供应商宣布的IPv4空间减少了18.5%。文章还提到具体受影响的公司和地区，如Donetsk、Lugansk、Mariupol和Kherson等地的网络供应商。

Summary
In this post, we discuss how the ongoing war in Ukraine has led to a significant decline in the amount of IPv4 address space announced by Ukrainian Autonomous Systems (ASes), and why those addresses are often now being announced by western ISPs and major public clouds.
The internet of Ukraine, noted for its resilience in the initial months following the Russian invasion, has been profoundly affected by three years of war. One notable change has been the exodus of a vital national commodity: IPv4 addresses.
In this blog post, we highlight several cases in which large amounts of IPv4 space, formerly originated by prominent Ukrainian ASes, have moved out of the country (often with the help of IPv4 brokers) to dozens of new origins, including major cloud providers, hosting operations, and international telecoms. The result is a dramatic reduction in Ukraine’s footprint in the global routing table — a new consequence of a protracted war in the digital age.

data.title: Revisiting the algorithm that changed horse race betting (2023)
data.author: areoform
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了比尔·本特（Bill Benter）通过在香港赛马中下注积累了10亿美元财富的故事。1994年，本特发表了一篇学术论文，详细介绍了他成功开发的赛马投注模型。尽管该模型可能因发表而失效，论文依然提供了对数学在赛马投注中应用的独特见解。本文提供了一个带注释的论文版本，并使用PyTorch重新分析了调整因素。论文探讨了数据需求、障碍模型开发、投注策略及可行性，并描述了一种结合基础障碍模型和公众隐含概率估计的logit技术。本特报告了该系统五年实际应用的显著成果，显示赛马投注存在 inefficiency。本文还讨论了技术系统与基础系统的区别，强调基础系统能提供更多高优势的投注机会。

主要讨论点：自动化赛马投注、算法与人类判断的优劣、赛马投注的实际可行性与风险

不同观点：
• **视觉观察的价值**：[AnotherGoodName] 认为自动化投注系统忽视了赛马当天状态的视觉信号（如马匹的活力和状态），而这些信号对于预测赛马表现非常重要。他以自己的农场经验为例，指出马匹的日常状态差异明显，任何纯算法的系统若不结合这些信号可能难以取胜。

• **算法投注的风险与局限**：[bitshiftfaced] 引用了Edward Thorp的经历，指出尽管算法投注能带来利润，但需要有人在现场下注，且面临持有大量现金的风险。此外，这种策略相比股票市场交易不够具有竞争力。

• **Dr. Z系统的实际应用**：[PaulHoule] 分享了自己使用Dr. Z系统进行赛马投注的经验，指出通过计算赢率和位置赔率的差异可以找到有利的投注机会。然而，这种方法每天只能使用几次，且总体盈利不多。

• **马匹状态与统计数据的对立**：[msarrel] 反驳了一些评论，认为马匹在比赛当天的外观和行为状态对于投注至关重要，单靠统计数据是不够的。

• **算法投注的普及与应对策略**：[jeffreyrogers] 提到算法投注在赛马中已非常普遍，占总投注的约40%。同时，[gosub100] 警告，如果找到盈利的算法，必须隐藏自己的投注行为，否则可能被赌场禁止参与。

• **赛马投注与股票投资的对比**：[WalterBright] 认为赛马投注是与“庄家抽水”对抗，而股票投资则是顺应经济增长，因此更偏好后者。

• **投注策略与自律**：[farceSpherule] 强调了制定并严格遵守投注策略的重要性，建议在赢得一定金额后停止投注，而不是继续冒险下注。

补充讨论：
• **具体案例与数据分享**：[elpakal] 提到一个案例，五季中有四季实现了净盈利，且随着模型的改进，收益率呈现上升趋势。

争议焦点：
• **视觉信号与算法分析的作用之争**：关于视觉观察（如马匹状态）是否能为投注提供额外的优势，存在不同看法。一方认为这是关键信号，另一方可能认为统计数据和算法足够。

• **算法投注的实际可行性与风险控制**：虽然算法投注能带来利润，但涉及的风险（如现场投注的风险、被赌场禁止等）也不容忽视。

44105470.article_content:
The remarkable story of Bill Benter and how he amassed a staggering $1B fortune betting on horses in Hong Kong has been extensively documented in the article,
The Gambler Who Cracked the Horse-Racing Code
1
. In 1994, Benter published an academic paper titled
Computer Based Horse Race Handicapping and Wagering Systems: A Report
2
. In it, he documents the implementation of a successful horse race betting model, which by virtue of it being published, likely meant that the model was outdated and superceded by more sophisticated models. Despite this, the paper remains an insightful read, offering a rare glimpse into the lucrative application of mathematics to an unconventional field, made even more interesting by the substantial hardware and software limitations of the time.
In this post, we present an annotated version of the paper with added code blocks and blockquoted comments. The main text is all from the paper itself. Instead of building the fundamental and combined models, we’ll be highlighting interesting aspects of the paper using the public estimate, derived from the
Hong Kong Jockey Club’s historical win odds
. We’ll look at how the model calibration tables were generated in the original paper, assess how the public estimate has improved through the years and try our hand at fitting the adjustments factors from scratch using PyTorch. While the original paper uses data samples between 1986–1993, we’ll also be using data from the subsequent three decades (1996–2003, 2006–2013 and 2016–2023) for comparison.

Abstract
This paper examines the elements necessary for a practical and successful computerized horse race handicapping and wagering system. Data requirements, handicapping model development, wagering strategy, and feasibility are addressed. A logit-based technique and a corresponding heuristic measure of improvement are described for combining a fundamental handicapping model with the public’s implied probability estimates. The author reports significant positive results in five years of actual implementation of such a system. This result can be interpreted as evidence of inefficiency in pari-mutuel racetrack wagering. This paper aims to emphasize those aspects of computer handicapping which the author has found most important in practical application of such a system.
Introduction
The question of whether a fully mechanical system can ever “beat the races” has been widely discussed in both the academic and popular literature. Certain authors have convincingly demonstrated that profitable wagering systems do exist for the races. The most well documented of these have generally been of the
technical
variety, that is, they are concerned mainly with the public odds, and do not attempt to predict horse performance from fundamental factors. Technical systems for place and show betting, (Ziemba and Hausch, 1987) and exotic pool betting, (Ziemba and Hausch, 1986) as well as the “odds movement” system developed by Asch and Quandt (1986), fall into this category. A benefit of these systems is that they require relatively little preparatory effort, and can be effectively employed by the occasional racegoer. Their downside is that betting opportunities tend to occur infrequently and the maximum expected profit achievable is usually relatively modest. It is debatable whether any racetracks exist where these systems could be profitable enough to sustain a full-time professional effort.
To be truly viable, a system must provide a large number of high advantage betting opportunities in order that a sufficient amount of expected profit can be generated. An approach which does promise to provide a large number of betting opportunities is to
fundamentally
handicap each race, that is, to empirically assess each horse’s chance of winning, and utilize that assessment to find profitable wagering opportunities. A natural way to attempt to do this is to develop a computer model to estimate each horse’s probability of winning and calculate the appropriate amount to wager.
A complete survey of this subject is beyond the scope of this paper. The general requirements for a computer bas

data.title: Personal Software Runtime Inspired by Emacs, Plan 9, Erlang, Hypermedia and Unix
data.author: veqq
data.article_summary:
**vrs** 是一个个人软件运行时环境，受 Emacs、Erlang、Unix、Plan 9 和超媒体系统的启发，旨在提供一个从编程语言、执行环境到编辑和工具的完整软件构建体验。其核心原则是 joy（愉悦）、uniformity（统一性）、simplicity（简洁性）、practicality（实用性）和 interactivity（互动性）。

**vrs** 包含以下组件：
- **lyric**：嵌入式 Lisp 方言及其虚拟机。
- **vrsd**：系统守护进程的运行时实现。
- **libvrs**：运行时和客户端实现共享的库。
- **vrsctl**：基于 **libvrs** 的轻量级 CLI 客户端。
- **vrsjmp**：GUI 启动栏客户端。

**Lyric** 语言示例展示了定义变量、函数、列表操作、条件判断、模式匹配等功能。软件在 **vrs** 中作为轻量级绿色线程进程运行，支持多核调度和非阻塞 IO。

项目仍在开发中，具有实验性质，存在不稳定和粗糙的部分。

In the multiverse, you can live up to your ultimate potential. We discovered a
way to temporarily link your consciousness to another version of yourself,
accessing all of their memories and skills.
It's called verse jumping.
— Alpha Waymond
What is this?
vrs
is a personal software runtime - an
opinionated take on my own "endgame" software platform.
It considers every aspect of programming - language, execution, environment,
editing, tooling, and more - designing across the end-to-end process of building
software.
Its inspirations are Emacs, Erlang, Unix, Plan 9, and Hypermedia systems.  It
hopes to combine powerful ideas from those projects into one cohesive whole for
an empowering, joyful, holistic programming experience.
The key principles are: joy, uniformity, simplicity, practicality, and
interactivity.
Status
🚧 Under heavy construction
🐉 Here be dragons
vrs is a sandbox project, focused on play and experimentation in a pure-fun,
pure-utility environment. While I live-on vrs everyday, the platform is very
volatile in both concepts and implementation.
This software has rough edges
. Be warned!
Structure
lyric
: Embedded Lisp Dialect and Virtual Machine
vrsd
: A runtime implementation as a system daemon
libvrs
: The
vrs
library crate shared by runtime and client implementations
vrsctl
: A thin CLI client over
libvrs
vrsjmp
: A GUI launch bar client
A Tour of VRS
Introduction to Lyric
The runtime runs software written in Lyric lang:
# Use `def` to define new bindings
# e.g. "hello lyric!" string to symbol `msg`
(def msg "hello lyric!")
# Update bindings with `set`
(set msg "goodbye lyric!")
# Basic Primitives - integers, lists, keywords, and more
42                                # integers
:my_keyword                       # keywords start with colon (:)
true                              # booleans are `true` or `false`
(list msg var_number var_keyword) # create new lists with `list` function
'("a" "b" "c")                    # quote expression with '
# Function declarationes use `defn`
# Lyric is expression-oriented - last form is returned as value to caller
(defn double (x)
(+ x x))
# Call functions by using bound symbol names within parens, followed by arguments
(double 10) # => 20
# List Operations
(def l '(1 2 3))
(def first (get l 0))       # get 0th item in `l`
(def last (get l -1))       # get last item in `l`
(contains? l 3)             # check if `l` contains `3`
# Association Lists
(def item '(:title "My Title" :subtitle "My Subtitle"))
(get item :title)      # => "My Title"
(get item :subtitle)   # => "My Subtitle"
# Functions (Lambdas) are first class
(defn apply (x fn)
(fn x))
(apply 41 (lambda (x) (+ x 1)))        # => 41
(map '(1 2 3) (lambda (x) (+ x x))     # => '(2, 4, 6)
# Conditionals with `if` - equality with `eq?`
(if (eq? msg "Hello")
"msg was hello"
"msg was not hello")
# and flip conditions with `not?`
(if (not? false)
"it was not true")
# Catch error with `try`. Introspect result with `err?` or `ok?`
(if (err? (try (not_a_function)))
"failed to call not_a_function")
# Pattern match with `match`. `_` is a wildcard pattern.
(def result '(:ok "Successful data"))
(match result
((:ok msg) msg)
((:err err) (:err err))
(_ '(:err "Unrecognized result")))
# Destructuring bindings can be used to pattern match against forms:
(def result '(:ok "Success"))
(def (:ok status) result)      # matches :ok, binds status to string "Success"
# As a Lisp, Lyric has `eval` and `read`:
(eval (read "(+ 40 2)")) # => 42
# and there are more builtins and symbols in environment, introspectable via `ls_env` and `help`
(ls_env)           # see all symbols defined in environment
(help recv)        # see documentation via `help`

Process
In VRS, software runs as
processes
running Lyric lang.
These processes are implemented as
green threads
,
and are lightweight compared to OS processes. Processes are scheduled on
multiple cores using nonblocking IO.
Each process has a single logical thread of execution. CPU-bound and IO-bound
work is transparent at process level, but the ru

data.title: After Deepfaking YouTube, Google's Veo 3 Could Slop-Ify Video Games Next
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 谷歌推出的Veo 3视频生成器能够生成不存在的3A游戏画面，引发了广泛关注。该工具可以根据提示生成逼真的游戏世界，如《侠盗猎车手》或《最后生还者》风格的场景。尽管涉及版权问题，但这些生成内容已被一些设计师整合进工作流中，通过其他3D工具进一步细化，实现高度定制。例如，设计师Lovis Odin展示了如何利用Veo 3生成的基础视频，结合其他工具进行3D渲染和细节调整。尽管目前AI尚无法生成完整的游戏代码，但谷歌早在2023年就提出，AI可以大幅降低游戏开发的劳动成本。然而，AI生成内容的质量参差不齐，可能对游戏行业从业者和游戏质量带来挑战。总体而言，AI在游戏开发中的应用潜力巨大，但同时也伴随着风险。

Google’s new video generator is out in full force, and I don’t know about you, but my feeds are
fullÂ
of examples of what it can (and sometimes can’t) do. I’ve already covered how it’s
deepfaking smooth-brain YouTube content
,
half-baked Michael Bay bulls**t,
and
absurd pharma ads
, but there’s another category I haven’t talked about yet, and it’s potentially a lot more impactful than the former uses. Sorry, gamers, but Veo 3 (and likely other video generators) might be on a collision course with your AAA games next.
Veo 3 does video games really well. It's like you can explore new worlds already.
Prompts are all variations of:
> a third-person open world video game walking around…
> an fps video game in/on a…
pic.twitter.com/bpDGaKNU55
— fofr (@fofrAI)
May 22, 2025
One area that Veo 3 is surprisingly functional at is generating
fake gameplay footage
of nonexistent AAA games, whichâif you’ll allow me to turn my brain off for a momentâis pretty entertaining. Above are the results of a prompt that asks Veo 3 to generate a third-person open-world game in different settings, including some realistic
Grand Theft Auto
-style generations, some sci-fi, some fantasy, and one that looks an awful lot like
The Last of Us
. Copyright concerns aside, it’s pretty neat!
It makes sense, given the never-ending stream of gaming content that Google might have at its disposal through YouTube, that Veo 3 would be able to spit out some kind of facsimile of a AAA game. That’s not the part that really intrigues me; it’s that people are already taking those generations and running with them. Below is an example from a 3D designer who goes by
Lovis Odin on X
demonstrating how Veo 3’s outputs can be integrated into a workflow that takes the AI video generator’s text-to-video powers and makes them even more granular.
Google Veo3 creates beautiful base videos, but what if thatâs not enough?
I built a
@ComfyUI
workflow that takes it further:
ð New structure with Flux (LoRA arch)
ð¦ Turned into 3D with Hunyuan3d 2
ð Integrated + relight via Flux, Controlnet, Denoise and Redux
ðï¸ Finalized theâ¦
pic.twitter.com/pAfu2qVU34
— Lovis Odin (@OdinLovis)
May 27, 2025
Using a few other tools in tandem with Veo 3, Odin takes an initial video prompt and then adds a structure that is rendered into 3D and is then fully customizable. Sure, Veo 3 can add objects on its own, but as Odin notes, what separates this workflow from your typical text-to-video prompt is the granularity. As good as text-based prompts can be, they’re also kind of a huge pain in the ass if you want something
specific,Â
which makes them less ideal for real, professional workflows.
Odin’s workflow isn’t solely focused on games, to be clearâthis is the type of thing that could be applied to really any generative videoâbut it feels especially practical for game development. Think about it: you have an idea, you generate the look with Veo 3, customize it with other 3D tools, and then (though this part isn’t included in Odin’s workflow) you bring it to life with AI-generated code. Obviously, this last part is the biggest piece of the puzzle, and generative AI isn’t quite at the level of being able to properly code AAA games yet, but that doesn’t mean we aren’t trending in that direction.
People are already well along on their journey to
“vibe coding” simple games
, but something tells me that’s just the beginning. Google itself already
broached the idea of generatively coded games
back in 2023, stating in a blog post on generative AI and gaming that “creating content is one ofâif not the largestâexpenses that games can incur.” The blog also said, “According to the UKâs CMA, blockbuster games can have development budgets well over $100 million… AI allows developers to leverage this new technology in a way which is respectful of intellectual property while protecting one’s own proprietary data.”
To summarize Google, if I may, game development is expensive and time-consuming, and they see big potential in reducing the labor costs of games, copyright be damned. Is that surprising? No, not at all. AI, if we’re to believe the hype, appears to be a labor-reducing force across the board in lots of industries, games included. What is surprising, however, is that the progress in that direction might be coming faster than we think, and if it’s really here, that could be bad news for the real, extremely overworked people of the games industry and potentially bad news for games themselves.
As vast as the potential for augmentative AI may be, the potential for
AI slop
is just as high, and unfortunately, there’s nothing special about the games industry that would prevent that same slop-like ripple from taking effect. I’ve learned not to sound the alarms too earlyâthings happen in the tech world, and they happen fast. Maybe in the not-so-distant future, we’ll wake

主要讨论点：对当前科技发展及AI作用的不同看法

不同观点：
• [surprisetalk] 分享了多个与其兴趣相关的深度科技链接，包括Terraform Industries、Third Law和Higher Order Co等在各自领域的工作，但没有直接表达个人立场或观点，仅提供信息分享。

• [cinbun8] 对[surprisetalk]的发言提出质疑，怀疑其是否为AI bot，并用戏谑的语气要求其说出“Watermelon”以验证身份。这一评论并未直接讨论科技发展，而是对其他评论者身份的真实性提出质疑。

• [throwaway314155] 认为近年来计算机科学领域没有出现大量真正新颖的发展，但对深度学习持积极态度，认为尽管存在过度炒作，但深度学习是令人兴奋的科技进步，并指出其根源可以追溯到20世纪50年代的图灵。评论者理解有些人对深度学习不感兴趣，但希望大家能理解深度学习爱好者的热情。

• [emursebrian] 介绍了自己正在开发的语言学习平台Emurse，强调了平台的实用功能和与内容创作者的合作。虽然认可AI的作用，但对当前泛滥的“AI垃圾”表示厌倦，主张通过与优秀内容创作者合作来提供高质量的学习资源。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点似乎并未集中在具体技术上，而是在于对AI和深度学习的态度。[throwaway314155]对深度学习持正面态度，而[emursebrian]则对AI相关内容的泛滥表示不满，更倾向于通过与真人创作者合作来提高内容质量。

• [cinbun8]的评论偏离了主题，更多是对其他评论者身份的调侃，未对科技发展提供实质性讨论。

• 总的来说，讨论展现了对当前科技发展的不同关注点和态度，有人关注深度科技的进展，有人对AI和深度学习充满热情，还有人更看重与人类创作者合作的价值。

44118632.article_content:
Europe can capture the US brain drain — if it acts fast
Download PDF
Twitter
Facebook
Email
You have full access to this article via your institution.
Download PDF
In the 1990s, I left Portugal to become a scientist. London, then New York City — at that time, I could find the financial support and intellectual environment I needed only by moving abroad.
Today, many scientists in the United States are experiencing
cuts to government research funding
and face
a similar reckoning
. I’ve seen the evidence. I’m now back in Portugal, working as chief executive of the Gulbenkian Institute for Molecular Medicine (GIMM) in Lisbon. In the past 2 months, more than 30 junior researchers at US institutions have written to me to ask about job opportunities — 10 times what I would normally expect.
European countries must work together to become the global destination for scientific talent.
How the United States became a science superpower — and how quickly it could crumble
Some efforts are under way
.
A European Union initiative offers incentives
and protections to researchers affected by political instability or funding cuts. Programmes in France aim to host displaced or returning scientists.
But most of these initiatives are fragmented. A coordinated strategy is crucial to lure the brightest minds.
CERN, the European particle-physics laboratory near Geneva, Switzerland, shows what can be achieved. It was created in the 1950s by physicists, who persuaded governments to invest in shared infrastructure and long-term collaboration. Now, it involves more than 12,000 scientists and thrives thanks to stable funding, open science and a culture of international partnership.
Similarly, programmes launched in the 1990s and 2000s made Canada a global research hub. Funding for national priorities such as environmental and genomics research was paired with competitive working conditions — including fast-tracked immigration and world-class infrastructure.
And
China’s Thousand Talents
and Ten Thousand Talents programmes have lured thousands of scientists with generous start-up funding — often exceeding US$500,000 and guaranteed for five to ten years — as well as the promise of autonomy over their research agenda and budget.
Cuts to US science will take a generation to repair — leaders must speak up now
How can Europe emulate these successes? More funding is key. Last year, two reports recommended that the budget for the European Framework Programme, which funds research and development across the EU, be doubled, from almost €100 billion (US$112 billion) for the 2021–27 cycle to between €200 billion and €220 billion for 2028–34 (see
go.nature.com/3zqdjte
and
go.nature.com/4mpgdgh
). This would enable institutions to offer competitive salaries, state-of-the-art infrastructure and long-term career support.

data.title: The Myth of Developer Obsolescence
data.author: cat-whisperer
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了技术发展对软件开发的影响，尤其是从无代码运动到人工智能辅助开发的演变。每次新技术出现时，都会有人宣称这些技术将使开发者过时，例如无代码工具、云计算和 offshore 开发等。然而，现实是这些技术并没有取代开发者，而是创造了新的专业角色和更高的薪酬需求，例如无代码专家和DevOps工程师。

人工智能辅助开发同样遵循这一模式。尽管AI能生成代码，但它往往需要高级工程师的校正和系统架构设计。软件开发中最有价值的技能不是写代码，而是设计系统架构，这是AI无法替代的。技术进步并未消除专业技能的需求，而是将其提升到更高的抽象层次。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在软件开发和系统架构中的作用以及对开发者工作的影响

不同观点：
• **whstl**：认为AI在处理复杂需求时会造成更多混乱，最终仍需要人类开发者来修复。强调开发者对不合理需求的拒绝能力是其重要资产，而AI可能会因为竞争而总是有人会答应不合理需求。
• **jstummbillig**：认为AI无法决定人的意图和目标，尽管AI在系统架构上已经显示出能力，但最终还是需要人类来推动事情的发生。
• **vinceguidry**：指出企业只关注利润而非质量，只有工程师在乎质量。因此，关于AI取代开发者的预测不切实际，因为质量不是企业的首要考虑。
• **fhd2**：提到过去几次非技术性的变革（如UML生成代码、敏捷转型）并没有真正解决问题，反而增加了复杂性。强调非开发者对开发工作的支持和参与是成功的关键。
• **dinfinity**：认为AI已经在系统架构设计上比一些人类架构师做得更好，文章没有提供足够的证据支持其观点。
• **crakhamster01**：担心过度依赖AI会导致产品质量下降，并引用微软GitHub的事故率作为例子，认为过度追求效率会损害质量。
• **nhumrich**：认为代码是负债而非资产，AI生成大量代码反而增加了负债，自然的约束减少了。
• **mpweiher**：引用FORTRAN的历史，指出对技术取代开发者的预言早已有之，但并未实现。
• **sunegg**：认为当前的AI在独立环境下表现良好，但在集成到完整技术栈时会失败，无法替代开发者。
• **overflow897**：认为如果技术持续进步，AI最终可能能够处理架构和长期规划，不能以当前的能力来判断未来的潜力。
• **janalsncm**：认为裁员主要是由于经济不确定性，而不是技术进步，技术只是事后 justification 的工具。
• **IshKebab**：认为尽管AI目前不能取代开发者，但未来5到10年可能会发生变化，不仅仅是开发者，其他岗位也可能被取代。
• **gherkinnn**：认为开发者的重要技能是将现实世界的复杂性翻译成计算机能理解的内容，而no/low-code平台和LLM在这方面表现不佳。
• **inadequatespace**：认为AI可能加剧不平等，创造出“低级”开发者或将工作外包给低薪国家。
• **JimDabell**：指出20世纪90年代就有预言WYSIWYG编辑器会使网页开发者过时，但事实并未如此。

补充讨论：
• AI在系统架构设计上的潜力与局限：部分评论认为AI已经能够胜任一些架构设计工作，但也有评论指出AI在处理复杂需求和集成时表现不佳。
• 企业对质量与利润的关注：有评论指出企业更关注利润，而非开发者关注的质量问题，因此AI取代开发者的前景可能被夸大。
• 历史视角：多次技术变革并未如预言般完全取代开发者，历史可能在AI时代重演。
• 不平等与就业影响：AI可能导致开发者之间的不平等加剧，或将工作外包给低薪国家。

争议焦点：
• AI能否真正取代开发者，尤其是在系统架构和复杂需求处理方面。
• 企业对质量与利润的不同关注是否会影响AI在开发工作中的应用前景。
• 技术进步与就业市场变化之间的关系，以及AI对就业市场的长期影响。

44105592.article_content:
From NoCode to AI-Assisted
Every few years, a shiny new technology emerges that promises to make software developers obsolete. The headlines follow a predictable pattern: "The End of Coding," "Anyone Can Build Apps Now," or my personal favorite, "Why Your Five-Year-Old Will Be Programming Before Learning to Read."
The executives get excited. The consultants circle like sharks. PowerPoint decks multiply. Budgets shift.
And then reality sets in.
What actually happens isn't replacement, it's transformation. Technologies that promised to eliminate the need for technical expertise end up creating entirely new specializations, often at higher salary points than before. The NoCode movement didn't eliminate developers; it created NoCode specialists and backend integrators. The cloud didn't eliminate system administrators; it transformed them into DevOps engineers at double the salary.
Now we're witnessing the same pattern with AI-assisted development. The promise that "AI will write all your code" is evolving into the reality that we need engineers who can effectively orchestrate AI systems, which is essentially the same engineers, but now with new skills and higher salary expectations.
But there's something deeper happening with this particular transformation. Unlike previous technological shifts that primarily changed how we implement solutions, AI-assisted development is highlighting a fundamental truth about software engineering that has always existed but is now impossible to ignore:
The most valuable skill in software isn't writing code, it's architecting systems.
And as we'll see, that's the one skill AI isn't close to replacing.
The Endless Carousel of Replacement Promises
How many times have we ridden this merry-go-round? Let's count the rotations:
The NoCode/LowCode Revolution
Remember when drag-and-drop interfaces were going to let business users build their own applications? The promise was clear: "Why hire expensive developers when anyone can build an app?"
What actually happened: These tools created a new class of problems. Someone still needed to design the data models underpinning those shiny interfaces, integrate with existing systems and databases, handle edge cases the visual tools couldn't address, and maintain and upgrade as requirements evolved.
The result wasn't fewer developers—it was the birth of "NoCode specialists" who understood both the business domain and the technical limitations of these platforms. And guess what? They commanded higher salaries than the developers they supposedly replaced.
The Cloud Revolution
"Move to the cloud and you won't need system administrators anymore!"
As if infrastructure would somehow manage itself once it was someone else's server. The cloud didn't eliminate the need for systems expertise. Instead, it transformed what that expertise looked like and dramatically expanded its scope.
The sysadmins weren't eliminated; they were reborn as DevOps engineers with fancy new job titles and substantially higher compensation packages. The work didn't disappear; it evolved into infrastructure-as-code, automated deployment pipelines, and distributed systems management.
As I noted in my
LinkedIn post about microservices
: "I've watched teams spend months decomposing perfectly functional systems into microservices only to discover they've traded one set of problems for a more expensive set." The cloud enabled this complexity and someone still needed to manage it. That someone was still a systems expert, just operating at a higher level of abstraction.
The Offshore Development Wave
"Why pay local developers when you can get the same work done for a fraction of the cost overseas?"
The promise of dramatic cost savings quickly collided with the reality of communication challenges, quality issues, and the discovery that effective software development requires deep contextual knowledge and continuous collaboration.
What emerged instead was a more nuanced approach: distributed teams with clear ownership boundaries, stronger architecture practices, and—surprise—higher total costs than initially projected.
The AI Coding Assistant Revolution
And now we have AI promising to write our code for us. "Just describe what you want, and the AI will generate it!"
The early reality is already emerging. AI generates plausible-looking code that often contains subtle inconsistencies and errors. Senior engineers spend significant time verifying and correcting AI output. The "vibe coding" phenomenon means experienced developers extract far more value than novices. Systems built entirely with AI assistance often lack coherent architecture.
"In the world of the chisel, you just gave carpenters a CNC machine. Guess who will make the better furniture?"
The pattern is becoming clear once again: the technology doesn't replace the skill, it elevates it to a higher level of abstraction.
Why This Time Is Different
Here's what the "AI will replace developers" crowd fundamentally misunderstands:

data.title: I salvaged $6k of luxury items discarded by Duke students
data.author: drvladb
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者住在杜克大学附近的一栋公寓楼里，那里常有学生在学年结束时丢弃大量物品。作者在垃圾房里发现许多完好无损、甚至未拆封的贵重物品，如高档衣物、家具和电子产品，其中一些价值不菲。作者收集并整理了这些被丢弃的物品，发现总价值约6000美元。同时，作者通过制作表格比较不同大学的捐赠数据，试图了解这种浪费现象是否普遍存在。尽管大量可用物品被丢弃令人震惊，但作者也感到不安，毕竟这些是他人丢弃的财物。公寓的维护人员对此表示理解，并允许作者随时到垃圾房捡拾有用物品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大学生在学年结束时丢弃大量物品的现象及其背后原因，奢侈品市场的人为稀缺性，以及垃圾回收和二手物品处理的实际操作。

不同观点：
• **奢侈品市场的虚假性**：[newccount] 认为奢侈品品牌通过销毁未售出的库存来人为制造稀缺性，并使用各种手段隐藏商品的真实产地，质疑奢侈品的实际价值。他们引用Cartier母公司销毁4亿英镑手表的例子来支持这一观点。

• **文化差异和物品处理方式**：[dkga] 提到在瑞士，人们通常会把不需要的物品放在路边供他人免费拿取，并对作者感到内疚表示不解。他们认为重复使用物品是一种积极的行为。

• **国际学生和搬家困难**：[matthewowen] 和 [AdmiralAsshat] 分享了作为学生在搬家时面临的实际困难，例如物品运输成本高、时间紧迫，导致不得不丢弃一些物品。[AdmiralAsshat] 特别提到自己曾被迫丢弃一个便宜的搅拌机，因为运输成本高于其本身价值。

• **垃圾回收和物品再利用**：[bityard] 和 [nappy-doo] 分享了在大学城通过垃圾箱寻找可用物品的经验，指出很多被丢弃的物品实际上仍然完好无损。他们认为这是一种资源再利用的方式。[alnwlsn] 进一步指出，不仅是学生，富裕地区的人们也常常丢弃稍有损坏但仍可修复的物品。

• **捐赠数据和未被统计的捐赠**：[Kon-Peki] 质疑文章中对学生捐赠量的统计数据，认为未被大学统计的捐赠，例如通过教堂和犹太教会进行的捐赠，可能未被计算在内。

• **市场流动性和二手物品买卖**：[the__alchemist] 提到买卖二手物品的不便之处，指出买卖之间的价差和流动性问题使得人们更倾向于丢弃物品而不是转售或捐赠。

补充讨论：
• **道德和法律问题**：[nancyminusone] 认为从垃圾中捡东西没有道德问题，只要明确物品是被丢弃而不是被误放。

• **实际案例和经验**：[xivzgrev] 和 [pknomad] 分享了自己或他人通过Craigslist转售被丢弃物品的实际经验，指出这种行为在学生中并不少见。

争议焦点：
• **奢侈品市场的真实价值和人为稀缺性**：有人质疑奢侈品市场通过销毁商品制造稀缺性和高价值形象，而其他人则可能认为奢侈品有其独特的市场需求和价值。

• **物品丢弃和再利用的文化差异**：不同地区和文化在处理不再需要的物品时的方式和态度存在差异，一些人认为重复使用是积极的行为，而另一些人则可能因为各种实际困难而选择丢弃。

• **二手物品市场的流动性和便利性**：买卖二手物品的实际操作中存在的困难和不便，使得人们更倾向于丢弃物品而不是转售或捐赠，这是另一个值得注意的讨论点。

44108207.article_content:
Illustration by Nicole Pajor Moore
I
live in an apartment building in downtown Durham that houses more Duke University undergrads than any other category of person—a friend once characterized it as an “adult dorm”—so it wasn’t all that surprising when, last week, I found a cute little table in the trash room on my floor. At the end of the school year, a lot gets thrown away.
The table was in great condition, amid stacks of linens and unopened boxes of date-nut energy bites. Made from clear acrylic, its edges were tinged a neon lemon-lime color that changed with the light—sometimes appearing to be part of the acrylic itself, other times a reflection dancing along its curves.
I took it home. When I looked it up online, I discovered it costs $900. (Shipping cost: $199.)
That was retrieved from the trash room at the end of my hall, where you put things down the chute. The real gold mine is the ground-floor room that the chute empties into, accessible by one of the elevators.
This is where, around graduation each year, you can find dozens of vacuums, Keurigs, stainless steel trash cans in every size and shape imaginable, mattresses, mirrors, and enough luxury goods to make a reseller weep with joy. The first time I went down there, last week, I noticed something neon in a tote bag and pulled out $395 Balenciaga slides. Nearby were $980 Valentino sneakers—worn, but definitely wearable. More than $1,000 of Lululemon workout clothing tumbled from a bag onto a couch.
Peek behind the Triangle scene.
Get curated coverage in your inbox every Friday.
Sign up
You don’t really have to do any digging—most of the stuff I’ve gotten was sitting on top of discarded furniture. But you do have to rush. After I took the Lululemon haul upstairs, I returned to find city waste workers loading things into a garbage truck, off to a landfill. The volume of discarded clothing seems consistent with generational trends: textile waste in the United States went up by more than 50 percent between 2000 and 2018.
The trash room. Photo by Lena Geller.
Not every treasure is a flashy brand-name item. I also recovered pink satin pajamas that I remember seeing on someone attending a pajama party on my floor, and a ruffled olive-green
Top Gun
romper from a Halloween event. (Sadly, there was nothing from the risqué Dr. Seuss party. A few months ago, a fire alarm went off, and it became apparent just how much of the building is occupied by Duke students, as nearly everyone except me, my roommate, and a family with two young kids was drunk and dressed in
Cat in the Hat
costumes.)
It feels wrong for this much stuff to have been thrown out in the first place, but it also feels mildly wrong to take it. So it was nice to get intermittent reassurance from my building’s maintenance man, Eric.
The first time, as I was scurrying back to my room, carrying an upholstered kitchen chair that my cats now spend all their time in, I passed Eric in the hallway. He asked me how I was.
“Just doing some scavenging,” I said. I must have looked guilty, because he said, “That’s OK.”
A few days later, I was again downstairs in the big trash room when Eric walked in. I moved to leave, feeling awkward about being caught again. “You’re welcome here anytime,” he assured.
The sheer volume of valuable, usable things being discarded boggles the brain, particularly when it comes to items like clothing with the tags still on and unopened, unexpired food items.
In trying to make sense of things, I made spreadsheets.
The first tracks the prices and brands of the items that I kept, donated, or sold. The total value came to around $6,000, not including several items I couldn’t find prices for.
A screenshot of one section of the author’s itemized spreadsheet
The second spreadsheet compares Duke’s donation collection data with that at other universities, in an effort to understand whether this college-town phenomenon is universal. I gathered publicly available data from university websites and press releases, supplemented by direct inquiries.
Duke told me their “Devils Care Donations” initiative collected 32,000 pounds this year through partnerships with TROSA and Goodwill. Ali Harrison, senior associate dean for residence life, says that the university places donation bins in every residence hall on campus, plus off-campus Duke housing like Blue Light and Swift Apartments. Harrison also notes that “Duke students who live off campus in non-Duke housing can schedule a TROSA pickup for large or bulky items and large donations.”
I emailed six universities, asking about their donation programs and collection data. Most didn’t respond or declined. One directed me to a public web page. Rice University, whose “Give a Hoot! Donate Your Loot!” campaign recently won a statewide award in Texas, sent a detailed response. They reported that they collected around 11,000 pounds of “durable goods” from students this year. data.title: A toy RTOS inside Super Mario Bros. using emulator save states
data.author: notorious_pgb
data.article_summary: 这篇文章通过在NES版《超级马里奥兄弟》游戏中实现多线程来解释线程的概念。作者将线程比作模拟器的存档状态，并展示了三个同时运行的马里奥游戏实例，每个实例分配不同的颜色调色板。线程调度器每160帧切换一次线程，跳过被杀死、阻塞或睡眠状态的线程。文章还介绍了同步原语，如互斥锁（Mutex）和条件变量（Condition Variables）。例如，当一个马里奥站在起点三个砖块上时，其他马里奥的游戏会暂停，直到他离开。通过这种方式，文章生动地展示了多线程编程中的时间分片、互斥锁和条件变量等概念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对线程、并发、实时操作系统（RTOS）以及相关概念（如互斥锁、信号量、协程等）的技术探讨和比喻解释

不同观点：
• Sohcahtoa82将线程、多核处理、互斥锁、信号量等概念用工具箱和工作台等比喻进行解释，强调了多线程和多核的区别，以及同步工具的使用场景。
• Ericson2314对Sohcahtoa82的解释进行了细化，指出线程和进程的区别主要在于通信和同步机制的不同，并提到通过改变模拟器的外部实现可以更接近硬件并发的支持。
• mort96提出了关于实时操作系统的疑问，认为在模拟器中实现实时性增加了复杂性，限制了调度算法和内存分配器的选择。
• Cloudef认为文章中描述的线程概念更像是协程或绿色线程，并指出它们的区别在于协同调度和抢占式调度。

补充讨论：
• noone_youknow对文章和线程比喻表示高度赞赏，认为这种解释方式有助于帮助人们更好地理解底层系统。
• ignormies回忆了大学时学习实时操作系统课程的经历，认为文章中的可视化演示非常酷，并表示希望找到一个小项目来再次探索这一领域。
• gwbas1c提到了一种消除模拟器延迟的方法，通过预计算不同按钮组合的状态，然后根据实际按键切换到预计算的状态，类似于文章中的线程概念。
• 其他评论如liamwire、Refreeze5224等对文章的可视化演示表示赞赏，认为有助于理解复杂的线程和调度概念。
• CGamesPlay建议如果子世界内存可以在保存状态之间共享，将更能体现互斥锁的概念。
• dsfdsfsfew认为文章在定义RTOS上有所扩展，虽然与预期的使用ACE运行并发程序不同，但仍然具有趣味性和信息性。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议点在于对线程和协程的定义和区分，Cloudef认为文章中的概念更接近协程，而Sohcahtoa82的比喻则更侧重于线程和多核的区别。Ericson2314进一步补充了线程和进程在通信和同步机制上的不同。

This is another post about programming, which I almost never write about.
Click here
to jump straight to trying this thing out for yourself.
In my
previous post
on Threads, I made an offhand comparison
1
:
Threads
2
are just emulator
3
save states
4
, coupled with a condition upon which they will be resumed.
At the  time, I thought this a
pretty
okay
analogy — but I couldn’t stop thinking about it. I’ve been turning it around in my mind for a while. I think it has serious untapped potential as a pedagogical tool.
So I added multithreading to
Super Mario Bros.
for the NES.
The Thing Itself
No buried ledes here.
What It Is
I should explain myself.
What you just watched happens to be a multithreaded NES emulation, with
Super Mario Bros.
as the threads.
There are three “threads” running, each a distinct instance of the game. Every so often, the emulator switches “threads”, swapping to a different instance of the game.
Each “thread” is assigned a different color palette, which we apply when we resume said thread. This is why the colors are constantly changing around in the video.
More Specifically…
When World 1-1 starts, the “multithreading” begins. Specifically, my script creates three
save states
, each representing the current state of the game
5
. Then I create three
threads
6
, and give them their respective save state to hold on to.
Then I start the thread scheduler.
The thread scheduler’s job is simple:
Every 160 frames, switch to a new thread
The next thread ideally, in a rotating fashion (1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 1, …)
Skip over threads which are
KILLED
,
BLOCKED
(unless they can be unblocked), or
SLEEPING
(unless it’s time to wake them)
To switch to a new thread:
First, update the
current
thread’s save state with the current game state
Then, load in the
new
thread’s save state
Finally, update the
game color palette
to reflect which thread we’re on
This covers what you see for the first bit of the video: each thread starts at the same time (the loading screen for World 1-1), with different “games” being swapped in every so often.
Essentially,
three different games of Mario Bros.
are being played “at the same time”, but only one is actually
active
at any given time.
Beyond Just Time Slicing
This image shows the full World 1-1 map, with color-coded areas indicating various features explained below. I recommend clicking to expand this image.
Time slicing is cool — we’re running three “concurrent” games of Mario! — but that’s far from the only threading concept demonstrated here.
I’ve set up the game world in such a way that certain areas or features activate synchronization primitives (such as a mutex); you can
physically interact with threading boundaries
.
I describe the synchronization primitives I’ve set up below, but the
net effect
is:
If a Mario is standing on the three blocks at the start of the level, no other Mario’s game will run until he leaves (
Disabled Interrupts
)
Only one Mario can be inside the Pipe Sub-level at a time (
Mutex
)
If a Mario enters while another Mario is inside, his game will not resume until the other Mario leaves
Once a Mario touches the flagpole, his game pauses until all the other Marios have touched their flagpoles (
Condition Variables
)
Disabled Interrupts
The red shaded area on the map denotes a section of the world where
interrupts are disabled
, and therefore, the thread scheduler cannot run.
Whenever a Mario enters the red shaded area, his thread won’t lose control until he leaves the area, regardless of what other Marios are doing.
Mutexes
The yellow shaded area (difficult to discern — it’s the fourth pipe from the left; the one you can go down) demonstrates a
mutex
: an area of the game world where only one Mario may exist at a time.
When a Mario goes down the pipe, he tries to acquire the
pipeMutex
. If nothing else owns that mutex (i.e., no other thread is currently in the pipe sub-level), then he immediately gains ownership of the mutex and proceeds without issue.
However, if another Mario owns the mutex (is presently in the pipe sub-level), then the Mario which is presently entering the pipe will be
blocked
until the mutex is released (the other Mario leaves the pipe sub-level).
Marios outside of the pipe sub-level are not blocked, and are still allowed to run.
Condition Variables
The green shaded area (the flagpole at the end of the level) demonstrates a
condition variable
: when a Mario touches the flagpole, he increments
numMariosTouchedFlagpole
— a “condition variable” — by 1, and then blocks until that same condition variable is equal to the number of threads. In other words, he waits until all the other Marios have touched the flagpole before continuing.

Whenever a Mario kills

• gwbas1c提到了一种消除模拟器延迟的方法，通过预计算不同按钮组合的状态，然后根据实际按键切换到预计算的状态，类似于文章中的线程概念。
• 其他评论如liamwire、Refreeze5224等对文章的可视化演示表示赞赏，认为有助于理解复杂的线程和调度概念。
• CGamesPlay建议如果子世界内存可以在保存状态之间共享，将更能体现互斥锁的概念。
• dsfdsfsfew认为文章在定义RTOS上有所扩展，虽然与预期的使用ACE运行并发程序不同，但仍然具有趣味性和信息性。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议点在于对线程和协程的定义和区分，Cloudef认为文章中的概念更接近协程，而Sohcahtoa82的比喻则更侧重于线程和多核的区别。Ericson2314进一步补充了线程和进程在通信和同步机制上的不同。

data.title: Prohibition and ice cream in the US Navy
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary:
**总结：**

1914年，美国海军通过《第99号总令》全面禁止舰艇上饮酒。此前，海军已逐步限制酒精，并在1914年彻底禁止在船上的任何地方饮酒。1920年，美国全国进入禁酒期，导致非法酒吧兴起，但意外促进了冰淇淋的流行，许多酿酒厂转为生产冰淇淋。二战期间，美国海军在太平洋战区使用专门的冰淇淋驳船，每天生产大量冰淇淋，以提高士气。冰淇淋成为奖励手段，特别是在救援飞行员时，船员会获得大量冰淇淋作为奖励。禁酒令期间及二战中，冰淇淋在海军中扮演了重要角色，甚至取代了传统的朗姆酒奖励。

44119173.article_content:
General Order 99
One hundred and eleven years ago on July 1, 1914, Secretary of the US Navy Josephus Daniels issued
General Order 99
, banning “the use or introduction for drinking purposes of alcoholic liquors on board any naval vessel, or within any navy yard or station.”
The US Navy had ended the rum ration in 1862 and imposed progressively more stringent restrictions on what alcohol sailors could have on shipboard. General Order 99 ended even the serving of alcohol in the wardroom and the captain’s cabin. An updated repost.
Prohibition and Ice Cream
Six years later, in 1920, the entire country followed the Navy’s example. With the ratification of the 18th Amendment, the United States banned the production, importation, transportation, and sale of alcoholic beverages. The thirteen year period known as
Prohibition
led to the growth of criminal gangs and the proliferation of “speakeasies,” illegal drinking establishments.
Prohibition also had a surprising and unexpected result — the growth in the popularity of ice cream. During Prohibition, many American breweries, including Yuengling and Anheuser-Busch, switched from brewing beer to making soda and ice cream. Ice cream parlors became popular places to socialize for both young and old. By the end of the decade,
Americans were consuming more than a million gallons of ice cream per day
—and, crucially, associating it with the comfort and diversion formerly assigned to alcohol.
World War II and the Navy’s Ice Cream Barge
With the end of Prohibition and the outbreak of World War II, the still dry US Navy was provided with ice cream on almost every ship.  In the Pacific theater of war, the US Navy even operated a large concrete
ice cream barge
. The Navy spent $1 million dollars retrofitting a barge they got from the Army to allow it to produce 10 US gallons of ice cream every seven minutes, or approximately 500 US gal per shift, and could store 2,000 US gallons of the finished product. Smaller barges, known as ice cream ships, were built to distribute the ice cream throughout the Western Pacific.
Ice cream was important for morale. In 1942, the U.S.S. Lexington was slowly sinking from a Japanese torpedo attack, before the crew abandoned ship,
they broke into the freezer and ate all the ice cream
. Survivors
describe
scooping ice cream into their helmets and licking them clean before lowering themselves into the Pacific.
Ice Cream as a Reward
In addition to the daily rum ration, when the captain of a naval sailing vessel wanted to reward the crew when things went exceptionally well, he might order a tot for all hands. The US Navy developed its own reward system. As there was no alcohol to be had, they used ice cream.
Ice cream became a reward for meritorious service. Specifically, on carriers, a reward system was set up for every pilot rescued by destroyers, escorts, submarines, or any other craft that brought a downed pilot back to the ship. During World War II; ten, twenty, or even thirty gallons of ice cream might be the payoff for a rescued pilot.
Tom Kocurko spent World War II
in the Navy and found out about the ice cream tradition while serving on a destroyer escort. “We’d get 10 gallons of ice cream every time we picked up a pilot, which was a real treat. So we started joking, ‘Let’s shoot one down.”‘
Sometimes ice cream may be better than even a tot of rum.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust调试工具的实用性、功能、兼容性及用户体验

不同观点：
• [mickey475778] 对工具表示期待，认为它可以有效解决Rust中所有权和异步并发调试的难题，但同时对工具在处理大型数据结构或长时间计算时的表现提出疑问。
• [orsenthil] 对工具的用户界面表示赞赏，并联想到自己使用的Pythontutor，暗示了对类似工具的熟悉和认可。
• [waschl] 对工具表示兴趣，但指出其无法与在qemu中运行的Rust操作系统内核一起使用，关注工具的兼容性问题。
• [tonyhart7] 希望将类似工具应用于数据库调试，关注查询检查功能，表现出对工具具体应用场景的兴趣。
• [forrestthewoods] 对工具在真实程序调试中的有效性持怀疑态度，认为仅演示玩具例子不具备说服力，强调对实际应用的支持和效果。
• [spencerflem] 对工具表示兴奋，联想到Glamorous Toolkit，并对"解释程序运行过程"类型的工具表现出兴趣，显示出对类似工具的开放态度。
• [quotemstr] 从调试器的角度出发，认为Rust只是另一种本地代码语言，DWARF可以提供必要的调试信息，暗示对专门为Rust设计的调试工具的必要性持怀疑态度。
• [Veserv] 将该工具与chrome://tracing等传统跟踪查看器进行比较，认为该工具的跟踪可视化密度低且缺乏有意义的执行时间信息，质疑其创新性和实用性。

补充讨论：
• [levkk] 表达了使用该工具的迫切需求，但遇到了安装脚本需要sudo权限和仅支持VSCode插件的问题，寻求其他使用方式的帮助。
• [dochtman] 关注工具在macOS和移动设备上的兼容性问题，并对网站的动画设计表示不满。

争议焦点：
• 工具在真实程序调试中的有效性和实用性。
• 工具的创新性及其相较于传统调试工具的优势。
• 工具的兼容性和用户体验问题，包括安装和使用上的障碍。

data.title: What does “Undecidable” mean, anyway
data.author: BerislavLopac
data.article_summary:
本文简要解释了“不可判定”（Undecidable）在计算机科学中的含义，特别是针对没有计算机科学背景但有些许好奇的读者。文章首先引用了一本名为《Automata and Computability》的书中的技术定义：一个字符串属性P是可判定的，如果存在一个图灵机能够对具有属性P的输入返回“true”，对不具有的返回“false”。

接着，文章将这一技术概念转化为程序员更容易理解的术语。它解释了在自动机理论中，程序的输入是字符串，输出是“true”或“false”。通过这种模型，可以研究不同计算能力的计算模型，包括有限状态自动机（DFA）和图灵机（TM）。

图灵机是计算能力的上限，如果一个问题图灵机无法解决，那么任何实际编程语言也无法解决。文章还提到，图灵机可以模拟其他图灵机的运行，这使得我们可以研究图灵机行为的相关决策问题，例如某个图灵机是否在十步内完成计算。

最终，文章通过具体例子帮助读者理解“不可判定”的概念，即某些问题是图灵机无法解决的，从而也是任何实际编程语言无法解决的。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不可判定性及其相关概念，包括计算理论、复杂性、逻辑独立性等。

不同观点：
• [mreid] 认为理解不可判定性的关键在于，并不是所有的 `f: string -> boolean` 函数都可以通过程序实现。由于程序是可数的无穷多，而函数是不可数的无穷多，因此存在无法通过程序表达的函数。这解释了为什么像 `IS_HALTING` 这样的函数不可判定。
• [Animats] 指出，任何具有有限状态的确定性系统都是可判定的，只有在无限内存的情况下，停机问题才不可判定。他认为文章没有明确区分复杂性和不可判定性，并强调复杂性（如P=NP问题）和不可判定性是不同层次的问题。
• [ummonk] 对“停机检测器可以被用作程序优化器/定理证明器/密码破解器/国际象棋引擎”的观点持怀疑态度，认为即便不通过停机问题，像密码破解和国际象棋等问题已经有相对简单的算法，虽然时间复杂度很高。
• [godelski] 认为要理解不可判定性，需要参考哥德尔不完备定理。他强调任何一致的公理系统都无法证明所有关于自然数的真理，总会有一些真命题是不可证明的。
• [taeric] 提出可以通过“欠指定”的概念来理解不可判定性，即在某些情况下，程序的部分可以被充分约束以回答特定问题，但其他部分可能仍然自由。
• [nialv7] 认为不可判定性与实数不可数性本质上是同一件事，但文章没有深入探讨这一联系。
